result.summary: 15 requirements (10 functional, 5 non-functional); 20 ambiguities resolved as assumptions (14 human decisions, 6 recorded defaults) and 1 remains open.

outputs.goal: Make the single-node shortener’s redirect behavior measurable and more robust, and apply the specified security controls without changing the behavior or retention of existing links. Do not attempt to fix an unconfirmed failure cause or expand the work to infrastructure or third-party systems.

functional.text: Preserve existing link behavior: every active link must continue to resolve to the same destination with identical behavior; expired links return 410 and deleted links return 404. Do not change link or tombstone retention.
Preserve the existing response contract: invalid input returns 400, unknown or deleted codes return 404, and expired links return 410. Return errors using the standard JSON error body.

When the database is unavailable during a redirect, return 503 with a Retry-After header and the standard JSON error body. For other unexpected errors, return 500 with the standard JSON error body and no internal details.
Limit request bodies for /api/** to 16 KB. Reject larger bodies with 413 Payload Too Large and the standard JSON error body.
Keep the existing link-creation limit of 20 creates per minute per client IP. Requests exceeding the limit return 429 with a Retry-After header and the standard JSON error body.

Limit failed management-token attempts to 10 per minute per client IP, counted across the stats and delete endpoints. Further requests during the limit period return 429 with a Retry-After header and the standard JSON error body.
Do not add a rate limit for link-code probing in this release. Redirect 404 metrics must remain aggregate and must not distinguish causes such as unknown, deleted, or wrong-case codes.
Expose redirect outcome counts and redirect timings through Spring Boot Actuator and Micrometer. Count redirect outcomes as 302, 404, 410, or 5xx; do not add per-cause breakdowns for 404.
Expose only Actuator health and metrics endpoints on a separate management port bound to 127.0.0.1. Keep the existing public /health endpoint on the main port unchanged.
Do not check whether link destinations are reachable and do not retry destination requests on behalf of clients.

non_functional.text: Return these security headers on every service response: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff; X-Frame-Options: DENY; Referrer-Policy: no-referrer; Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'.
Do not add visitor data to logs.

While the service and database are available, an active link must not receive a 5xx response. The existing in-process redirect p99 < 50 ms check must continue to pass. A database outage returning 503 is the specified exception.
Limit changes to the url-shortener service running as a single node. Do not change infrastructure, deployment systems, or third-party integrations.

The release gate is that all existing and new tests pass, the test suite contains at least the current 95 tests, security headers and error behavior are covered by automated tests, and the product owner approves the release.

ambiguities.question: Which pre-existing links are in scope, and for how long must they continue to work (including expired, deleted, or otherwise inactive links)?
ambiguities.resolution: Every active link keeps resolving to the same destination with identical behaviour. Expired links keep returning 410 and deleted links 404, as today. No change to how long links or tombstones are retained.
ambiguities.rationale: Decided by a human: This defines the compatibility requirement and retention scope for existing links.

ambiguities.question: Which reliability measures and targets define “more reliable” (for example, availability, resolution success, latency, or recovery time)?
ambiguities.resolution: Measure redirect outcomes and latency through Spring Boot Actuator and Micrometer: count redirects by outcome (302, 404, 410, 5xx) and time them. Target: an active link never receives a 5xx while the service is running, and the existing in-process redirect p99 < 50 ms check keeps passing.
ambiguities.rationale: Decided by a human: These are the measures and targets to use; the database-outage exception is clarified separately.

ambiguities.question: What failures have users experienced, how often do they occur, and which shortener workflows or user groups are affected?
ambiguities.resolution: There is no incident data, only anecdotal reports. The goal is to make failures measurable and diagnosable (per-outcome redirect metrics, consistent JSON errors), not to fix a guessed bug. Likely causes to confirm with the metrics: expired links (410) and aliases typed with the wrong case.
ambiguities.rationale: Decided by a human: Do not treat anecdotal causes as confirmed defects or expand scope to fix a guessed bug.

ambiguities.question: What threats, attackers, and attack surfaces must the security work address, and what residual risk is acceptable?
ambiguities.resolution: Address a public-internet attacker who probes codes and management tokens, floods link creation, sends oversized or malformed requests, or tries to extract internal details from errors, as well as browser-side framing or content-sniffing attacks. Accepted residual risk: no URL reputation or malware scanning of destinations and no authentication system beyond management tokens.
ambiguities.rationale: Decided by a human: This sets the threat model and accepted residual risks for this release.

ambiguities.question: Which security controls or data-handling requirements are expected, including requirements for access, privacy, logging, or compliance?
ambiguities.resolution: Add the specified standard security headers to every response, enforce a request body size limit for the JSON API, and ensure errors never include stack traces or internal details. Log nothing new about visitors. Actuator exposes only health and metrics endpoints. No compliance regime applies to this release.
ambiguities.rationale: Decided by a human: These controls and data-handling expectations are binding for this release.

ambiguities.question: Which service components, integrations, and deployment environments are in scope for reliability and security changes?
ambiguities.resolution: Only the url-shortener service, running as a single node. No infrastructure, deployment or third-party integration changes.
ambiguities.rationale: Decided by a human: This limits implementation scope to the service itself.

ambiguities.question: What should happen for failed, malformed, unknown, or unreachable links, including response behavior, status codes, and retry behavior?
ambiguities.resolution: Keep the existing contract: 400 for invalid input, 404 for unknown or deleted codes, and 410 for expired links. If the database is unavailable during a redirect, return 503 with a Retry-After header and the standard JSON error body instead of an unhandled 500. Any other unexpected error returns a 500 JSON error without internal details. The service never checks whether a destination is reachable and never retries on the client's behalf.
ambiguities.rationale: Decided by a human: This specifies the required response and retry behavior; the precise 503 Retry-After value remains open below.

ambiguities.question: What broader-rollout decision or release gate must the reliability and security work satisfy?
ambiguities.resolution: All existing tests and the new tests pass, the suite must not drop below its current 95 tests, security headers and error behaviour are covered by automated tests, and the product owner approves the release.
ambiguities.rationale: Decided by a human: These are the required release gates.

ambiguities.question: What maximum request-body size should the JSON API enforce?
ambiguities.resolution: 16 KB for requests to /api/**, well above the largest valid create request. A larger body is rejected with 413 Payload Too Large and the standard JSON error body.
ambiguities.rationale: Decided by a human: This sets the API request-body limit and oversized-request response.

ambiguities.question: What controls and thresholds should protect against link-code or management-token probing and link-creation floods, including the response to requests that exceed those limits?
ambiguities.resolution: Keep the existing limit of 20 creates per minute per client IP (429 with Retry-After). Add a limit of 10 failed management-token attempts per minute per client IP, counted across the stats and delete endpoints; further attempts get 429 with Retry-After and the standard JSON error body. Add no link-code probing limit in this release; the accepted residual risk and its observability are as stated in the requirement.
ambiguities.rationale: Decided by a human: These thresholds, responses, and the decision not to limit link-code probing are binding.

ambiguities.question: Who may access the Actuator health and metrics endpoints?
ambiguities.resolution: Only operators on the host. Serve the Actuator endpoints on a separate management port bound to 127.0.0.1, so they are unreachable from the public interface and no new authentication system is needed. The existing public /health endpoint on the main port stays as it is.
ambiguities.rationale: Decided by a human: This defines management endpoint access and preserves the existing public health endpoint.

ambiguities.question: What is the standard JSON error-body schema, including its fields and message format?
ambiguities.resolution: Keep the existing contract {"error": "<stable machine-readable code>", "message": "<human-readable text>"} and use it for every error response, including framework-generated errors such as unmatched routes, 405, 413, 500 and 503.
ambiguities.rationale: Decided by a human: This establishes the required error-body schema and its coverage.

ambiguities.question: Does the target that an active link never receives a 5xx while the service is running exclude database outages, or must the 503 database-unavailable response be changed?
ambiguities.resolution: The target applies while the service and its database are available: then an active link never receives a 5xx. During a database outage the 503 with Retry-After is the intended, explicit behaviour.
ambiguities.rationale: Decided by a human: The reliability target excludes database outages, for which 503 is intentional.

ambiguities.question: Must redirect metrics distinguish 404 causes, such as unknown codes, deleted codes, or aliases entered with the wrong case, or is an aggregate 404 outcome sufficient?
ambiguities.resolution: An aggregate 404 outcome is sufficient. No per-cause breakdown: it would add queries on the redirect hot path and record more about requests than needed. Diagnosing wrong-case aliases is out of scope for this release.
ambiguities.rationale: Decided by a human: Use aggregate 404 metrics only and leave wrong-case diagnosis out of scope.

ambiguities.question: How should “16 KB” be counted at the request-body boundary?
ambiguities.resolution: Treat the limit as 16,384 bytes of request body, excluding headers; reject bodies larger than that with 413 and allow bodies at or below the limit to proceed to normal validation.
ambiguities.rationale: A byte-based 16 KiB limit is a conventional, unambiguous interpretation of an API body-size limit and is low risk.

ambiguities.question: How should the service determine a request’s client IP for per-IP rate limits?
ambiguities.resolution: Use the remote address of the connection. Do not trust caller-supplied forwarding headers unless an existing, explicitly trusted proxy configuration is present.
ambiguities.rationale: Using the connection peer unless a trusted proxy is configured is the conventional secure default and avoids spoofable client-supplied addresses.

ambiguities.question: Which requests count as a failed management-token attempt?
ambiguities.resolution: Count a stats or delete request rejected because its management token is missing or invalid; do not count requests rejected for unrelated reasons.
ambiguities.rationale: Counting authentication failures, rather than unrelated request errors, is the conventional interpretation of failed token attempts.

ambiguities.question: How should the new management-token per-minute window and its Retry-After value be calculated?
ambiguities.resolution: Use a rolling 60-second window per client IP. When the limit is reached, return Retry-After as the whole number of seconds, rounded up, until another attempt is permitted. Preserve the existing link-creation limiter’s current window behavior.
ambiguities.rationale: A rolling 60-second window directly enforces the stated threshold; a seconds-based Retry-After is a conventional HTTP representation. Preserving the existing creation limiter avoids changing its current behavior.

ambiguities.question: What Content-Type should error responses use?
ambiguities.resolution: Use Content-Type: application/json for every response carrying the standard JSON error body.
ambiguities.rationale: application/json is the conventional media type for the specified JSON response body.

ambiguities.question: What stable error-code and message mapping should be used for the error-body schema?
ambiguities.resolution: Preserve existing error-code values where they already exist. For newly normalized error cases, use stable lowercase snake_case codes corresponding to the category (for example, method_not_allowed, payload_too_large, rate_limited, service_unavailable, and internal_error). Use concise human-readable messages that contain no internal details.
ambiguities.rationale: Stable lowercase category codes and concise generic messages are conventional and preserve existing code values while covering newly standardized framework errors.

ambiguities.question: What TCP port should the local-only Actuator management listener use?
ambiguities.resolution: Use 8081 as the default separate management port, configurable through the service’s existing configuration mechanism, and bind it to 127.0.0.1.
ambiguities.rationale: 8081 is a conventional alternate application port; keeping it configurable makes the default low risk while ensuring it is separate from the main listener.

ambiguities.question: What Retry-After delay or date should the 503 response use when the database is unavailable?
ambiguities.rationale: The human decision requires a Retry-After header but does not specify its value. Guessing a retry interval could cause clients to retry too aggressively or wait unnecessarily during a database outage.

acceptance_criteria: Given a previously active link, when a client follows it, then it redirects to the same destination with the same behavior as before; expired links return 410 and deleted or unknown codes return 404.
Given an invalid API input or malformed request, when it is submitted within the body-size limit, then the service returns 400 with a JSON error body containing error and message fields.
Given an unmatched route or unsupported method, when requested, then the service returns 404 or 405 respectively with the standard JSON error body.

Given a request to /api/** with a body larger than 16,384 bytes, when submitted, then the service returns 413 with the standard JSON error body; a body at or below the limit is not rejected solely for size.

Given a database outage during a redirect, when the redirect is requested, then the service returns 503 with a Retry-After header and the standard JSON error body. The Retry-After value is blocked on human clarification.
Given an unexpected server error, when it occurs, then the service returns 500 with the standard JSON error body and does not expose a stack trace or internal details.

Given a client IP that exceeds the existing link-creation limit, when it submits another create request within the applicable limit period, then the service returns 429 with Retry-After and the standard JSON error body.

Given 10 failed management-token attempts from one client IP within a rolling 60-second window across the stats and delete endpoints, when further stats or delete requests are made before an attempt is permitted, then they return 429 with Retry-After and the standard JSON error body.

Given redirect requests with 302, 404, 410, or 5xx outcomes, when metrics are inspected through the local Actuator metrics endpoint, then redirect counts by those outcomes and redirect timings are available; 404 is not broken down by cause.

Given a request from a non-local interface to an Actuator endpoint, when it is made, then the endpoint is unreachable; from the host, only Actuator health and metrics endpoints are exposed. The existing public /health endpoint continues to behave as it did before.
Given any service response, when its headers are inspected, then it includes the specified X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, and Content-Security-Policy values.
Given an error response, when its body and headers are inspected, then its Content-Type is application/json and its body has the standard error and message fields with no internal details.
Given the service and database are available, when an active link is redirected, then the response is not 5xx; the existing in-process redirect p99 < 50 ms check continues to pass.

Given the release candidate, when the release gate is evaluated, then all existing and new tests pass, the suite contains at least 95 tests, security headers and error behavior have automated coverage, and product-owner approval is recorded.
